[2026-09-20T19:52:24+00:00] PAID-FOR TRAP, measurement not code: a computed opacity read less than a frame after a class change returns the value the transition STARTED from, and on this harness a frame is ~1s — so a 450ms wait, and even a settle-poll at 150ms intervals (two reads inside one frame compare equal and look settled), reported the ghost fade as not firing at all. Three probes chased a CSS rule that was correct from the first write; the engine's own rule list (w.matches over document.styleSheets) is what settled it. Read a transition's end state after >1 frame, never after its declared duration, and never trust a settle-poll whose interval is shorter than a frame. The fade arm in verify-gamepad waits 2600ms for this reason and says so.

[2026-09-21T08:07:03+00:00] A FADE MUST NAME EVERY ELEMENT THE THING IS MADE OF. The ghost stick is THREE elements — the frame .ml-pad-stick with its .ml-pad-well and .ml-pad-top inside, plus .ml-pad-blur, a separate body-parented disc at z 3 that carries the backdrop-filter and has no background of its own. A fade scoped to '.ml-pad-stick .ml-pad-*' therefore hid the paint and left the LENS, and the report came back the same day: 'its blurry and make the background blurry'. The disc had never carried an opacity or a transition at all, since nothing had ever asked it to disappear. Two structural notes for anything that hides the ghost in future: opacity 0 does kill a backdrop-filter (the filtered backdrop composites through the element's opacity), and the disc cannot be reached from the stick's own .held because body.append(padBlur, pad) puts it FIRST — any held/hidden state it needs has to be published on :root.

[2026-09-21T15:58:06+00:00] A GUARD THAT ARMS LATE IS A RACE, AND THE SECOND OPEN IS WHERE IT SHOWS. The keyboard hold keyed off :root.ml-kb-up, which armLift sets — but arming at focus is one-shot: sync()'s 'open' is (r >= KB_MIN || shrunk >= KB_MIN || (!sawReport && touchDevice())), so once a session has seen one keyboard the lift stops assuming and waits for evidence, and the browser's page shrink arrives first. The resize then laid the game out for the short viewport (rail 540 -> 279) and the menu appeared between the input and the keys; worse, that layout overwrote layoutH, which layoutShrunk() subtracts from, so the shrink read 0 and the lift never armed at all for the rest of the session. Two rules out of it: a hold must start on the earliest SYNCHRONOUS signal the user gives (focusin on the tap), never on a state some later handler sets; and a measurement's baseline must be a value nothing else writes — kbBaseH is captured at focus while not holding, so a re-tap with the keys up cannot adopt the shortened viewport as 'no keyboard'.
